name: Gumbel-Asymmetric Power Loss
tagline: Expectile-weighted loss with super-quadratic exp penalty when V > Q and a power-1.5 |·|^1.5 penalty when V < Q.
formula: $$\ell(d) = \begin{cases}\big(e^{\alpha\,d}-\alpha d - 1\big)/\alpha^2 & d>0\\|d|^{1.5} & d\leq 0\end{cases},\;\;d=V-Q,\;\; \mathcal{L} = \overline{w(d)\,\ell(d)}$$ where $w(d) = (1-\tau)$ if $d>0$, else $\tau$

key_hyperparams.name: diff clamp
key_hyperparams.role: stability cap on positive diff before exp

init_recovers: Quadratic expectile when α→0 and p=2
diff_from_baseline: Vs expectile (default) and quantile_regression: keeps expectile asymmetric weighting (1-τ above, τ below) but replaces the quadratic above with an exponential (e^{αd}-αd-1)/α^2 penalty (super-quadratic, harshly punishing V>Q) and the squared below with |d|^{1.5} (between L1 and L2).

name: Soft-Expectile Log-Cosh
tagline: Log-cosh base loss with sigmoid-soft asymmetric weighting (smooth around d=0).
diff_from_baseline: Vs expectile (default) and huber_pinball: replaces the indicator-based hard weighting and squared/Huber base with log-cosh base loss and sigmoid-of-d/T 'soft' asymmetric weighting that varies smoothly through d=0; output is normalized by the mean weight to keep loss scale stable.

name: Stable Gumbel Regression (X-QL)
tagline: Replaces expectile with Gumbel-regression loss β·(exp((Q-V)/β) - (Q-V)/β), linearized above x=3 for stability.

key_hyperparams.name: linearization point c
key_hyperparams.role: x above which exp is replaced by tangent line

key_hyperparams.name: quantile arg
key_hyperparams.role: asymmetry parameter not used in this loss

init_recovers: X-QL log-sum-exp objective; reduces to the soft-max of Q at large data
diff_from_baseline: Vs expectile (default): does NOT use the IQL expectile; instead implements Extreme-Q-Learning's Gumbel-regression objective β·(e^{(Q-V)/β} - (Q-V)/β), with a clipped+linearized exp above x=3 for numerical stability. The quantile argument is not used.

name: Boundary-Focused Pseudo-Huber Expectile
tagline: Pseudo-Huber base, expectile asymmetry boosted near-boundary by exp(-|d|/scale) and modulated by a batch conservative-gap term.
formula: $$s = \overline{|d|}\;(\geq 10^{-3}),\;\bar n = d/s,\;\ell = s^2(\sqrt{1+\bar n^2}-1),$$ $$w = w^{\text{exp}}\!\cdot\!\big[1 + \mathbb{1}[d<0]\cdot e^{-|\bar n|}\,(0.75 + 0.75\cdot \rho)\big],\;\rho = \tfrac{\mathrm{ReLU}(\overline{Q-V})/s}{1+\mathrm{ReLU}(\overline{Q-V})/s}$$
init_recovers: Standard expectile with pseudo-Huber base when boost=1
diff_from_baseline: Vs expectile (default): batch-normalizes the residual by mean |d|, replaces squared loss with pseudo-Huber √(1+x²)−1, and multiplies the expectile weight with an adaptive boost that emphasizes small underestimation (V<Q, |d|≈0) more, modulated by the batch's conservative gap (Q-V)/scale.

name: Self-Calibrated Huber-Expectile
tagline: Asymmetric Huber with β set to median(|d|) per batch (clamped) and weight smoothly damped on large outliers.

key_hyperparams.name: β bounds
key_hyperparams.role: Huber transition point clipped from median|d|

init_recovers: huber_pinball baseline at β=1 and modulator=1
diff_from_baseline: Vs huber_pinball: makes the Huber transition β data-adaptive (median |d| clamped to [0.05, 5.0]) instead of a fixed beta=1, and multiplies the expectile weight by 0.8 + 0.2·min(1, 2/(1+|d|/β)) so very large residuals are slightly down-weighted to avoid outlier dominance.
